evidence.limits: Accepted-to-client-completion includes queue/callback overhead. No join was dispatched in that trace; it cannot prove current join latency. max4 concurrent slots is source capacity, not observed backlog.

source.owner_policy: Before each queued scan, njs_owner_work defers if any slot QUEUED/RUNNING; join blocks all new scan admissions. Owner can drain up to4 preadmitted scans.

assessment: Four scans at the observed all-channel2.134s duration sum8.536s before any join/auth/key work. Thus source-admissible backlog can exhaust8s, and even a single scan timeout can do so. It is not established as a practical observed current blocker: measured pending peak is1, usual13/9 scans finish~1.25/~0.9s. No new field or speculative RF command is justified.
safe_queued_priority_option: Under NSS admission lock, once join admission succeeds, mark only NSS_QUEUED slots canceled (or use existing nss cancel semantics atomically); leave NSS_RUNNING untouched. Keep slots/cookies/callbacks owned. Existing owner loop then takes canceled queued slots and invokes nss_deliver NSS_CANCELED without nss_execute; callbacks occur outside lock and must remain exactlyonce with existing deferred release. Do not zero slots or call callbacks inline; do not abort running firmware scan. Join remains pending until all these callbacks retire from queue.
recommendation: Safe bounded prioritization option if root wants to avoid a concrete worst-case budget conflict, but not demonstrated necessary to fix the no-SET20 failure. Current CARD gate is independently proven. Let current active scan drain; do not widen into firmware scan abort/reset. First station attempt remains unused if queued join times out before prepare.
operations: Read-only analysis of existing immutable log/source; no implementation/test/device/CI changes.
